newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends with pared gains before house data.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends with pared gains before house data.

text.p: CME lumber futures slipped from best levels in light dealings and ended with pared gains as profit taking developed ahead of Tuesday's monthly U.S. housing starts report, traders said.
Lumber closed $5.00 higher to $10.00 lower, with untraded distant July limit down on an offer. Nearby July ended up $4.80 at $373.90 per tbf, with September $1.30 firmer at $355.80.

Nearby July drew early support from talk Canadian mills may be reducing production due to slowing demand for lumber, while back months were buoyed by concerns over labor negotiations at British Columbia mills, traders said. The union said if there was no clear indication of progress by early July, it would consider a strike vote.
But profit taking ahead of the housing starts caused futures to drift back late, they said.

Estimates for May housing starts in a Reuters survey averaged 1.47 million units in a range of 1.42 to 1.50 million units and compared with 1.473 million the previous month. But traders said much of the talk they were hearing pointed to a 1.45 million unit start figure.
